INTRODUCTION
            I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs, having been authorised by
the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Sixty-first Report on the Demands for Grants (2000-2001)
relating to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs.

discussed the Demands and other related matters at its meeting held on 30 March 2000.

(i)                 Presentation made by the Secretaries/concerned officers of the related Departments;
(ii)               Detailed  Demands for Grants of the Ministry for 2000-2001;
(iii)             Annual Reports of the Departments for the year 1999-2000;
(iv)             Explanatory Note on the Demands received from the Ministry;
(v)               Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its Fifty-sixth Report on the Demands

(vi)             Written replies furnished by the Ministry on the Questionnaires sent to it by the Secretariat; and
(vii)           Written clarifications on the points/issues raised by the Members in the meeting of the Committee.
4.         The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on  10  April 2000.

2.                  The main functions of  the Department of Legal Affairs are :-
(i)                 To render advice to the various Ministries/Departments of the Government of India on   legal matters.
(ii)               To carry out the conveyancing work of the Central Government;
(iii)             To attend to the litigation work in the Supreme Court, High Courts, Tribunals and some of the subordinate courts;
(iv)             To handle the treaties and agreements with foreign countries in matters of Civil Law;
(v)               To authorise officers to execute contracts and assurances of property on behalf of the President under Article 299 (1)
of the Constitution and to sign and verify plaints and written statements in suits by or against the Union of India;
(vi)             To sanction grants-in-aid to certain institutions engaged in research  in the field of law.
2.1.      The Department of Legal Affairs is further  concerned    with appointment  of the Law Officers, namely the Attorney-General
of India, the Solicitor-General   for India and the Additional Solicitors-General for India, etc.   It administers the Advocates Act,
1961,  the Notaries Act, 1952 and the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.  The Department is also administratively incharge of the
Foreign Exchange Regulation Appellate Board, Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, Indian Legal Service and Law Commission of 
India.
2.2       The Department has a two-tier  organisational set-up, namely, the main  Secretariat at  New Delhi and the Branch Secretariats
at Mumbai, Calcutta, Chennai and  Bangalore.
3.                  The Legislative Department  deals with the following  matters:-
(i)                 Scrutiny of Notes for the Cabinet in relation to all legislative proposals  from drafting and constitutional points of
view.
(ii)               Drafting of all Government Bills including Constitution   (Amendment) Bills  before  introduction in Parliament;
translation of all such Bills into Hindi and forwarding both English and Hindi versions of the Bills to the  Parliament 
Secretariats; drafting of official  amendments to Bills, Scruting of non-official amendments and rendering   assistance
to Administrative Ministries to decide on the acceptability or otherwise of non-official amendments;
(iii)             Rendering assistance to Parliament and Joint Select or Standing Committees of Parliament at all stages through
which a bill passes before enactment.   This includes scrutiny of and /or preparation of reports of such Committees,
and Hindi translations of such reports and minutes of dissent;
(iv)             Drafting of Ordinances to be promulgated by the President;
(v)               Drafting of legislations to be enacted as President’s Acts in respect of States under President’s rule;
 
(vi)             Drafting of Regulations to be made by the President;
(vii)           Drafting of Constitution Orders, i.e. Orders required to be issued under the Constitution;
(viii)         Scrutiny of all statutory rules, orders and notifications and their translation into Hindi;
(ix)             Scrutiny of State Legislations in the concurrent field which requires assent of the President under Article 254 of the
Constitution;
(x)               Scrutiny of legislations to be enacted by Union Territory Legislatures;
(xi)             Elections to Parliament, Legislatures of States and Union Territories and Offices of the President and Vice-
President;
(xii)           Apportionment of expenditure on elections between the Centre and the States/Union Territories  with Legislatures;
(xiii)         Election Commission; Electoral Reforms;
(xiv)         Publication of Central Acts, Ordinances and Regulations and their authorised translations in Hindi and other
languages specified in the Eighth schedule to the Constitution.
4.         The Department of Justice deals with the constitutional organisation of the Supreme Court and the High Courts and the
appointment of Judges thereto, conditions of their service and with the administration of Judicial services in the Union Territories. 
Besides, it is the nodal Department in so far as the administration of justice in States is concerned, although the actual responsibility
of judicial administration below the High Court level rests with the concerned State Governments and High Courts.  Though this
Department forms a part of Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs, it is under the administrative control of Ministry of
Home Affairs.  Till 1992-93 the budget of the Department of the justice was salary oriented.   From 1993-94,  the Demands of the
Department of Justice also included provision for the Centrally Sponsored Scheme relating to infrastructural   facilities for the
judiciary and National  Judicial Academy.  From the financial year 1996-97 provision has also been made for the First National
Judicial Pay Commission, in the year 2000-2001, Rs.63.00 lakhs has been allocated for the Commission.
5.         The functions of the Department of Company Affairs in the Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs includes
administration of the Companies Act, 1956 and the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 for development and
efficient functioning of the Corporate Sector comprising Joint  Stock Companies.  The Department also exercises supervision  over
the activities of Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, Institute of Company Secretaries of India and Institute of Cost & Works
Accountants of India.  These Institutes, which are self-supporting, are concerned with the proper growth of profession of Chartered
Accountants, Cost Accountants and Company Secretaries.   The Department also has the responsibility of carrying out the functions
of the Central Government relating to the Administration of the Partnership Act, 1932, the Companies (Donations to National Funds)
Act, 1951 and Societies Registration Act, 1860.  Certain essential amendments to the Companies Act, 1956, initiation of modern

DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AFFAIRS
10.1     The Secretary, Department of Legal  Affairs made  a presentation   before  the Committee on 30th March, 2000. 
Appointment of  Notaries
11.       The  Committee, in its 56th Report on the Demands for Grants  of the Ministry for the year 1999-2000, had recommended   to
avoid long and undue delay in the appointment of Notaries and expedite the process in a definite time frame.  In its action taken reply
the Department  has  informed the Committee that it  has set up a separate Notary  Cell   to curtail the delay in appointment   of
Notaries.  In order  to assess suitability  of the applicants  for  appointment  as Notaries, the competent   authority  in this Department
earlier  used  to interview   the applicants.   However, this practice has since been dispensed with.  This step has been taken with a
view to curtailing  the delay in appointing Notaries.  On being asked whether with the setting   up of a  separate Notary Cell and with
the simplification of the procedure for appointment of Notaries, the pendency   has gone down  the Committee has been informed
that  prior to the  implementation of
 
the new decision for appointment   of Notaries, 935 applications were pending.  At present, 1693 cases for appointment of Notaries
are pending out of which 958 applications have been received during the period from June, 1999 to till date.   So far 200  Notaries
have been appointed.  With the dispensing of holding of interviews and with the gearing of the administrative   machinery, the time
taken for processing  the applications   for appointment of Notaries, has been reduced   considerably.   However, large number of
applications for appointment  of Notaries are being received  as  a result of which the pending applications have increased.  Since the
new system was introduced only in June, 1999, it would gradually knock  down  the pendency.
11.1     The Committee does not find the pending position with regard to the applications for appointment of Notaries
satisfactory.  It reiterates its earlier   recommendation  and hopes that the Government would ensure the quick disposal of
applications for appointment of Notaries and feels that if a definite time frame is fixed for disposal of applications it will
considerably reduce the pendency. The Committee further recommends that Government should ensure due representation
of Schedule Castes, Schedule Tribes and Other Backward Classes while appointing Notaries.
Law Commission
12.       The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory body constituted   by the  Government  from time to time.  The Commission
was originally constituted  in 1955.  It is reconstituted  every three years.  The present Law Commission (15th Law Commission) was
constituted  with effect from 1 st September, 1997 for a period of three years i.e. upto 31 August  2000.  The Committee has been
informed that the Commission  has so far submitted 171 reports, 91 of which have already been implemented.   32 reports have not
been accepted by the Government.   One report of the Commission is currently under   process for being laid in the Parliament.   The
remaining  47 reports are pending  for implementation/consideration with various Ministries/Department of the Government which
are administratively concerned with the subject matter of the reports.  The Government has further informed   that the Fifteenth Law
Commission has so far submitted fifteen Reports.  Fourteen reports have already been  laid in  Parliament.   The last Report is the
171st Report entitled “Bio-Diversity Bill”, received on 20.1.2000.
12.1     The Committee in its 45 th Report on Demands for Grants of the Ministry for the year 1998-99 had recommended to ensure
the accountability of the administrative Ministries of the Government for implementation of the accepted recommendations.    The
Committee reiterated  its earlier recommendation in its 56th Report  and desired that the concerned  Ministries/Departments might be 
persuaded and periodical meetings with them may be called once in a month to look into the  progress in that regard .  In any case 
accountability  may be fixed by the Government in cases where the concerned   Ministries/Departments have not started the
implementation  of the accepted reports of the Law Commission.  As regards reports relating to the subjects falling under List III of
the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution  of India, the Committee recommends  that the matter may be  taken up on priority basis
with the State Governments/Union Territories  Administrations  and it should be impressed  upon them to implement those reports in
a time bound manner.  In its action taken reply, the Department has intimated   that  the matter regarding early implementation of the
pending reports of the Law Commission is being pursued vigorously  with the concerned Ministries/Departments at the level of Law
Secretary.

National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and Lok Adalats
13.0     The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), a statutory   body constituted   under the National   Legal Services
Authorities Act, 1987 ( as amended   by the Act of 1994) is responsible    for extending   free legal assistance to poor and weaker
sections of the society entangled in litigation before  various  courts including   Supreme Court .  Rs.6.00 crore has been provided as
grants-in-aid for the  various  functions of the NALSA which inter alia
   include   organising  Lok Adalats and legal aid  to the
persons declared eligible under the Act.
13.1     The Committee , in its 45 th Report   had recommended   to lay the Annual Report  and Audited  Statement of Accounts of
NALSA on the  Table of the Houses  of Parliament.   In its action taken reply the Department   had stated    that the action for
submission of Annual Audited  Statement  of Accounts  of NALSA would  be possible only after the form and the manner in which
the Accounts  were to be  maintained  as well as the modalities   of the Legal   Aid Fund  are finalised   in consultation   with the
Comptroller  and Auditor-General of India and the Comptroller-General of Accounts .  The Department   had further replied   that as
decided in the first  annual  meeting of NALSA held on 13.9.97, the  modalities   for handling  and operation of the Legal Aid Fund
were worked  out  by a Committee and submitted to the Ministry  of Finance (Department of Expenditure) as far back as 29 th 
January, 1998 and the matter is still  pending with them even after being constantly  pursued  by the Department.
13.2     The  Committee in its 56 th Report, had reiterated its earlier recommendation and recommended   that the Annual Report and
Audited Statement of Accounts of the NALSA should be laid before the Parliament without further delay. In its action taken reply,
the Department has informed that the NALSA has requested the Ministry of Finance    (Department of Expenditure) to expedite its
recommendations on the modalities for handling and operation of the Legal Aid Fund.  The Member Secretary, NALSA has
addressed a letter on 3.6.1999 to the Additional Secretary, Department of Expenditure to submit their recommendations to the
Executive  Chairman of NALSA at the earliest so that a final decision in regard  to the handling and operation of the National   Legal
Aid  Fund as well as the modalities for submission of accounts and audited report to the Parliament can be taken.   As there has been
no response from the Ministry of Finance to the aforesaid   communication, Law Secretary   has addressed a d.o. letter to the
Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance on 16.9.99 to look into the matter personally and have 
necessary action in this regard expedited.   The Department has further informed that the Secretary, Department of Expenditure   has

13.9     There are several different and newer ways of settling disputes both quickly and inexpensively to avoid long, expensive and
enormously complicated procedures for seeking legal redress through judicial courts.  One such method is Lok Adalat.  Lok Adalats
which were initially started and encouraged by a few judges of the Supreme Court in October-November, 1985 as a way of
promoting voluntary  settlement of disputes  inexpensively and expeditiously have got the statutory status under the Legal Services
Authorities Act, 1987 which covers Legal aid, Lok Adalats and Legal Assistance Services and intends to secure the operation of the
legal system in order to promote social justice, particularly for the weaker sections of the society who because of economic and other
disabilities can not   afford the costs or delays involved in normal court procedures.  The jurisdiction of Lok Adalats is very wide. 
They can determine and arrive at compromises or settlements between the parties to a dispute in respect of  any matter  falling within
the jurisdiction of civil, criminal or revenue courts or tribunals.   The award of the Lok Adalat can be enforced in law as it is deemed
to be a decree of a civil court or tribunal and such
 
award is final and binding upon all parties in dispute to avoid further costs,  expenses and delay.   No appeal has been  provided from
such an award to any court.  The Lok Adalat has been given the powers of civil court under the Civil Procedure Code while trying
disputes and the proceedings before the Lok Adalat are deemed to be the proceedings of a court as provided in Indian Penal Code.

15.       The Committee has been informed that the Government has constituted   ‘The National Commission to Review the working
of the Constitution’ on 22 February 2000 to review the Constitution  of India  in the light of more than 50  years of its working and to

basic structure or features. The Commission shall decide its own procedure and hear and entertain all persons, representations   and
communications  which in the opinion of the Commission shall facilitate its work and finalise recommendations.   The Commission

wing on the domain of the others resulting in erosion of institutionalised arrangements which was not contemplated by the makers of

overlapping of the jurisdiction.

foresee it and rationally deal with it in advance.  But, retirement is known in advance.  In the past the Committee has time
and again   observed that the  process for filling up the vacancy must start considerably in advance before the actual date of
retirement of a Judge which would cause the vacancy.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the process of filling in
the vacancy should be initiated in such a manner that the vacancy is filled on the day it occurs.

huge amount on travel to reach the Supreme Court. There is a practice of bringing one’s own laywer who has handled the

Affairs should be provided a plan budget of Rs.100 crores at Revised Estimates stage so that it may undertake major project
